So I recently put together a new(used) home stereo system and have a question that I had no idea where else to ask. I have a technics sa-dx940 receiver and am wondering how would I go about connecting it to output to my speakers. Obviously I need some kind of preamp/converter to change the audio coming out of my phone to a CD, DVD, or aux signal the receiver will take. Ideas goats? Edit: thanks guys for helping my dumbass out!
A question for you audio pros and know-it-alls out there
It seems from this you can connect speakers directly in the back.
Sorry if I wasn't clear. I already have speakers setup playing from a turntable. What I want to do is connect my phone to the reciever.

Your phone have bluetooth? Maybe try looking at a "bluetooth music receiver" (Search on amazon, can't link to amazon on voat)

Maybe something like "Belkin F8Z492ttP Bluetooth Music Receiver"

(It uses an aux jack)

Turns out they all use a 3.5mm aux jack that my receiver doesn't have. I think the only way would be something that outputs like a CD player (preferably in optical) and let's me input from my phone. I think its a pretty specific use case :/
Came here to suggest the same thing.
The turntable should not be direct to speakers. It should go to the reciver, who handles speakers with amplification. As for the phone, @sapo has that part covered.
Unless it has a preamp installed already. Granted yes it wound sound as good as a solid state or tube amp but it should work.

There exists an adapter cord that has a 3.5 mm stereo jack (basic headphone plug) on one end, and a RCA split on the other (Red/White 1/8" plugs, your basic analog component interface). Slam the 3.5 in your phone and the RCA in any component input on the back of your reciever, and you be jammin, homie.

Better signal processing than a bluetooth, and much cheaper as well.
I saw that and wondered if there would be any interference issues but I think I'll give it a try since I'm working on the cheap. Thanks

The signal out of your phone is sent at what's called 'line level', an unamplified analog elecrtical waveform. It goes through shielded adapter cord at low amplitude into any digital processing your reciever provides, then into the amplification transistors, and on from there through shielded, stranded speaker wire to your transducers.

i.e. unless there is a break in the shielded signal path from the phone to your speaker cone, interferce would be nominal, whatever the tolerance is allowed for by that particular manufactuer.
Worst case scenario if it doesn't work is you blew a few bucks on an adapter chord. I'm in a similar situation and I was surprised by the quality of sound using an 3.5mm to RCA adapter chord.
